ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the breast

s1.syndrome_frame: a postmenopausal woman with a long-standing, progressively enlarging breast mass associated with skin ulceration
salient_findings: mass is hard, non-tender, and mobile
skin breakdown with mild exudation and bleeding
key_facts: 56-year-old postmenopausal woman
right breast mass noted for more than 1 year
mass has gradually enlarged
mass is hard in texture
mass is non-tender
mass is mobile
skin ulceration with mild exudation and bleeding
no palpable axillary or supraclavicular lymphadenopathy
breast ultrasound and MRI classified the lesion as BI-RADS category V
chest CT demonstrated a right breast mass suggestive of malignancy
serum breast tumor markers were within normal limits

shortlist.label: Invasive ductal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: most common type of breast cancer, consistent with long-standing, enlarging mass and skin ulceration

shortlist.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: aggressive type of breast cancer, consistent with skin ulceration and rapid progression

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a hard, non-tender, and mobile breast mass, along with skin ulceration and a BI-RADS category V classification on ultrasound and MRI, is most consistent with invasive ductal carcinoma, which is the most common type of breast cancer and can cause skin changes and ulceration, especially in advanced cases.

rejected.label: Inflammatory breast cancer
rejected.why: While inflammatory breast cancer can cause skin changes, it typically presents with rapid onset of erythema and edema, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Paget's disease of the breast
rejected.why: Paget's disease typically presents with eczematous changes of the nipple and areola, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Phyllodes tumor
rejected.why: Phyllodes tumors are typically large and rapidly growing, but they are less likely to cause skin ulceration and are often benign.

rejected.label: Metaplastic carcinoma
rejected.why: Metaplastic carcinoma is a rare type of breast cancer that can have a variety of presentations, but it is less common than invasive ductal carcinoma and the clinical features do not specifically suggest this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma of the breast
rejected.why: Angiosarcoma is a rare and aggressive type of breast cancer that can cause skin changes, but it is much less common than invasive ductal carcinoma and the clinical features do not specifically suggest this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lobular carcinoma
rejected.why: Lobular carcinoma is often multifocal and bilateral, and it is less likely to cause skin ulceration than invasive ductal carcinoma.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma of the breast
rejected.why: Squamous cell carcinoma of the breast is extremely rare and the clinical features do not specifically suggest this diagnosis.
